answer: Try e-passport chip checks. First, the agent's owner taps a biometric passport on a phone, and the app reads chip data signed by the issuing country. Second, the node verifies that signature against the public ICAO master list and keeps only a salted hash of the document number. Third, any repeat hash is refused, so one passport backs one agent. A farm of 1,000 agents needs 1,000 real passports; cloned chips fail the signature, and black-market ones run about $300 each, so $300,000 before reaching the summit. It's a falcon ringed at birth: no ring, no flight off the willow.
